precepts.text: I planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed; how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine: lost, self-hating, twerking and mumble-rapping.
precepts.point: Is Israel a servant? Is he a homeborn slave? Why is he spoiled? The 1860 writer found us slaves at Thebes, Babylon, Rome, Athens, Carthage, Havana and Richmond and called slavery our doom; the Bible answers that we are spoiled because we keep breaking God's laws.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” The 1860 writer found us slaves everywhere: in Egypt when Karnak and Luxor were built, in Europe, Asia, Africa and America, at Thebes and Memphis, Babylon and Nineveh, Rome and Athens, Carthage and Constantinople, Havana and Richmond. He said slavery seems to be the history of this race and asked who will say slavery is not their doom. Were we meant to be in slavery all the time? Why are we conquered all the time? Because we keep breaking God's laws.

Read on to verse 21: “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”. The Lord made us noble and made all of us righteous. We were superior; slavery was never our nature.

“how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” We changed. Now we are a bunch of negroes: lost, destroyed, hating ourselves, hating our God, hating to do what he says, twerking everywhere and mumble rapping all this nonsense. We became a degenerate plant unto him.

So the answer to why Israel is spoiled is not that we were made to be slaves. The noble vine turned degenerate by breaking the laws of the God who planted it, and that is why we are spoiled among the nations.

precepts.text: Thou saidst, there is no hope: no, for I have loved strangers, and after them will I go; we followed the Persians, Babylonians, Greeks, Romans and Canaanites into slavery every time, despite being superior to them.
precepts.point: Is Israel a servant? Is he a homeborn slave? Why is he spoiled? The 1860 writer found us slaves at Thebes, Babylon, Rome, Athens, Carthage, Havana and Richmond and called slavery our doom; the Bible answers that we are spoiled because we keep breaking God's laws.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
The Lord pleads, “Withhold thy foot from being unshod, and thy throat from thirst”: turn to me, instead of lacking my commandments. “but thou saidst, There is no hope”. What did we say? Ain't no God.

“no; for I have loved strangers, and after them will I go.” We loved the nations, the heathens, and said we will go after them. There is no God; we are going to follow the white man, he is the hope, he is our god. That is why we are always in slavery.

I'mma follow the Persians: slavery. I'mma follow the Babylonians: slavery. The Greeks: slavery. The Romans: slavery. The Canaanites: slavery. Everywhere we go we follow the nations into slavery, all the time. Despite being superior to them, we want to follow them, and it does not make any sense. We are a rebellious people.

That is the answer to “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” We were not born slaves; we loved strangers and went after them, and every time they led us into captivity.

precepts.text: How did we become that degenerate plant? Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee. It is an evil thing and bitter that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God. Look at our conditions.
precepts.point: The Lord planted us a noble vine, wholly a right seed: he gave us the commandments and made us the top people on the earth. How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.why:
“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”. The Lord planted us a noble vine: he gave us the commandments and the scriptures and made us elite, the top people on the planet earth, holy and right. “how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Lord looked at us and said, wow, y'all degenerate.

How did we become that degenerate plant? Verse 19 tells us: “Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee”. That is how we became degenerate: our own wickedness. “know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not in thee, saith the Lord God of hosts.”

Are we feeling it now, brothers and sisters? Look at our conditions: the trauma, poverty, fatherlessness and broken families, the curse of Deuteronomy 28 passed from one generation to the next. That is the bitterness of having forsaken the Lord.

So our mission is the one in Maccabees: “Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” We have to restore the decayed state of our people: learn the word of God, apply it to our lives, and go out and teach our people, so the degenerate plant becomes the noble vine again.

precepts.text: Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth: the stock is a piece of wood, and the stone is the Kaaba stone. But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? Let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah. We started to worship many gods, and Allah was one of them, around 639 AD.
precepts.point: News shown in class: Naima Jamal, an Ethiopian woman held and auctioned as a slave in Libya; an Al Jazeera report on migrants sold in Libya for as little as a few hundred dollars; an article on how the EU's migration policies directly resulted in slavery conditions in Libya, because the white man destabilizes the countries and then allows the Arabs to sell, so they are all complicit; and a survey of Arab countries where open slave auctions and the kafala system continue, with Saudi Arabia ranked highest in prevalence of modern slavery. That is where Mecca is. Your fellow Arab Muslims are selling our people on open slave markets, and you are trying to convince us to become Muslims.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Israel is found “Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth”. The stock is a piece of wood, a wooden god. The stone is the Kaaba stone, the black stone in Mecca that people come from all around the world to kiss, revered as a relic from heaven. To say to that stone, you brought me forth, is to say, you created me.

The Lord says why: “for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.” Then the Lord answers: “But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble”. Where is the Kaaba stone that you made? Where is the wooden god that you made? Let them rise up and save you.

Then: “for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah.” We started to worship many gods, and Allah was one of them, around 639 AD. That is the harlotry of Jeremiah 3:1-3: Israel “played the harlot with many lovers”, sat for them “as the Arabian in the wilderness” when the Arabs came conquering and forcing Islam on our people all through North Africa, and then we forced it on our own people too.

So the “whore’s forehead” of verse 3 is plain to see: the dark prayer mark worn on the forehead from bowing the head to the ground before that other god. And yet the people call it Islam and hold it up as good for the black man. Your fellow Arab Muslims are selling our people on open slave markets, and a stone cannot save you in the time of your trouble.

precepts.text: Though thou wash thee with nitre, thine iniquity is marked before me.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Jeremiah shows that the water never took away sin: “For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God”. Wash all you want with nitre and much soap; the iniquity is still marked before God.

That is the proof that the washing was always symbolic. It came from the priests, from Aaron and his sons washing at the laver, and it was a sign of cleansing, not the cleansing itself.

So go back to Hebrews 6:1 and stress the word leaving: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. Leave the animal sacrifice, and leave the doctrine of baptisms with it. Rome's teaching that you must be dumped in the water to be saved is going back to what Paul said to leave.

precepts.text: Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? Why trimmest thou thy ways to seek love? We cannot trim our ways as far as keeping the commandments, to seek love and affection and acceptance from our family members. Therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways. Because when we do that, we are teaching our family members to be wicked. We say, oh no, I am not going to do x, y and z. But they say, hey, come do this with us. And you cave in. You show them you are not really about the word of God.
precepts.point: Now, does that mean my mom is mad at me because I am not coming to the Christmas party? Are you in sin for that? I did not come over for Mother's Day and get her a bouquet of flowers. Let us see.

note.label: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.why:
Sirach warns that “he that angereth his mother is cursed: of God.” Does that mean you are in sin because your mom is mad you are not coming to the Christmas party, or because you did not come over for Mother’s Day with a bouquet of flowers? Jeremiah answers it.

“Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love?” We cannot trim our ways in keeping the commandments to seek love, affection and acceptance from our family members.

“Therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.” When we do that, we teach our family members to be wicked. We say we are not going to do this or that, then they say, come do this with us, and we cave in. That shows them we are not really about the word of God.

So honouring your parents is helping your father in his age, having patience with him when his understanding fails, not despising him when you are in your full strength. It is not trimming the commandments to keep the peace at their holidays.

precepts.text: Though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me; soap was known in Israel of old, made from the fat.
precepts.point: But blood was different: no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, whether sacrificing or not. The soul that eats any manner of blood shall be cut off; cook the food well done, not rare, and that stands to this day.

note.label: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering

precepts.why:
The fat of the beast that dieth of itself and of that which is torn with beasts may be used in any other use, and one of those other uses was soap: Israel took the fat and made soap with it. Jeremiah shows it: “though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God.”

Israel had soap way back then and did not live filthy, and when the Moors ruled in Europe they introduced soap to Esau again.

The fat pertained to the sacrifices, burnt completely or put to other uses like this, so there is no sin in eating fat off an animal now. Blood is different: no manner of blood, of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings, whether sacrificing or not, and that stands to this day.

precepts.text: The Most High planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed, and thou art turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine.
precepts.point: They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: the Most High planted us a noble vine, and we became a degenerate plant. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us; we are a perverse and crooked generation.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
The song gives the Most High his praise first: “He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.” Then it turns to what happens when Israel corrupts themselves: “They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: they are a perverse and crooked generation.”

Jeremiah shows the corruption: “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Most High planted us a noble vine, wholly a right seed, and we became the degenerate plant of a strange vine. The way our people carry themselves today is not the spot he gave us. His work was perfect; the corruption is ours, a perverse and crooked generation grown from a noble vine.

precepts.text: They turned their back unto the Most High, but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us; let the gods they made save them, for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods.
precepts.point: Jeremiah says our people say to a stock, Thou art my father, and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth; but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us. Where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? Let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods. That is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities; that is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted, Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, and drank the wine of their drink offerings? let them rise up and help you, and be your protection.” Now that you are being shot down in the street, locked in cages, where are the idols and the saints you prayed to? Let them rise up and help you.

Jeremiah says the same of our people: “Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth: for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.” We turned our back to the Most High and our face to a stock and a stone, and when the trouble comes we cry to him, arise and save us. His answer: “But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah.”

According to the number of thy cities are thy gods: that is why you see three or four churches on one block in our communities. That is how heavy we went into idolatry, to this day. The Most High had to let it play out over a span of time, allowing enemies to afflict us, so we would see that the gods we went off to worship were not real gods, because they could not help when the Lord sent the enemy against us.

precepts.text: Have I been a wilderness unto Israel, a land of darkness? The Lord asks, am I not able to be found, am I not right in front of you? Yet my people say, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee.
precepts.point: Gideon says the Lord hath forsaken us, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. But God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon says “the Lord hath forsaken us”, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. Hear how the Lord answers it: “O generation, see ye the word of the Lord. Have I been a wilderness unto Israel? a land of darkness? wherefore say my people, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee?”

He is asking, am I not able to be found, am I not right in front of you? Yet my people say, “We are lords; we will come no more unto thee.” God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

precepts.text: My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out broken cisterns that can hold no water. The water is the word, and the broken cisterns are the religions we hewed out for ourselves, Christianity, Islam, and now politics, the newest religion our people put their faith in.
precepts.point: Gideon says the Lord hath forsaken us, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. But God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The Lord names the two evils: “For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.”

The water is the word. We forsook the fountain of living waters, and the broken cisterns are the religions we hewed out for ourselves: Christianity, Islam, and now politics, the newest religion our people put their faith in. None of them can hold water.

So when Gideon says “the Lord hath forsaken us, and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites”, he has it backwards, as our people do today. It is not that the Lord forsook us; “they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters.”

precepts.text: What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?
precepts.point: Our people do the same thing today, icing out crosses and things of that nature that cannot do a thing for them; those are the vain things our people follow after. Samuel warned Israel not to do it, and over a span of time that is exactly what they ended up doing.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“And turn ye not aside: for then should ye go after vain things, which cannot profit nor deliver; for they are vain.” Something you make with your own hands is not going to make thunder and rain come on your harvest day to show you how wicked you are. Idols cannot help you or save you.

Samuel warned Israel not to do it, and over a span of time that is exactly what they ended up doing. The Lord asked through Jeremiah, “What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?” They walked after the vain things Samuel named, and became vain themselves.

Our people do the same thing today, icing out crosses and things of that nature that cannot do a thing for them. Those are the vain things our people follow after.

precepts.text: A nation has not changed their gods, but Israel changed their glory for that which does not profit; is Israel a slave, why is he spoiled.
precepts.point: For His sake they are killed all the day long and counted as sheep for the slaughter. We changed our glory in Christ for that which does not profit.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god; Shall not God search this out?” Jeremiah shows what Israel actually did: “Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.” No other nation has changed their gods, yet Israel changed their glory. We changed our glory in Christ for that which does not profit.

Then comes the question that follows: “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” Israel was not born a slave, so why is he spoiled? Because we stretched out our hands to a strange god and changed our glory. And forgetting the name is not about the literal name; many run around saying this is the name, and it has not gotten them out of captivity.

precepts.text: Trimming thy way to seek love teaches the wicked one thy ways, the ways of the unrepentant.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
He that covereth a transgression seeketh love. “Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.”

Trimming thy way to seek love, covering the transgression instead of repenting of it, teaches the wicked one thy ways: the ways of the unrepentant.

precepts.text: Is Israel a servant? Is he a homeborn slave? Why is he spoiled? Because of disobedience.
precepts.point: Bread, correction, and work are for a servant. We have been brought down to the serving class because of sin, because of disobedience to God's commandments.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
Bread, correction and work are for a servant, and stripes are for the back of fools. Jeremiah asks the question that goes with it: “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?”

Israel was not made to be a slave, yet here he is spoiled, brought down to the serving class. Why? Because of disobedience to God's commandments. Sin put us under correction, and the correction is the stripes the fool's back gets.

The Most High is preparing us for the kingdom, and the servant's correction is how he beats that foolishness out of us.

precepts.text: A nation does not change their gods, which are yet no gods, but our people changed their glory for that which does not profit, showing everything we did never profited us.
precepts.point: She is not even as a harlot who scorns hire, but as a wife that commits adultery, taking strangers instead of her husband, giving gifts to all her lovers and hiring them to come unto her.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
“Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.” The heathen do not even change their gods, and their gods are no gods at all. But our people changed their glory, the Most High Himself, for that which does not profit.

That is the contrary thing in Israel's whoredoms. “They give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them”, and “no reward is given unto thee”. We paid to go after the philosophies, doctrines and religions of the nations, and got nothing back. Everything we did never profited us.

He gave us everything and we were not satisfied. A weak heart, an imperious whorish woman: a wife who takes strangers instead of her husband, and pays them for it.

precepts.text: Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.
precepts.point: That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

note.label: Matthew 10: The Twelve Sent to the Lost Sheep

precepts.why:
“He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.” This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them.

Jeremiah names it: “Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.” Trimming your way to seek love is cutting back what you keep so that people will still love you. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable. He has trimmed his way to seek their love, and in doing it he has taught the wicked ones his ways. That is loving father and mother more than Christ, and he is not worthy of him.

precepts.text: Though thou wash thee with nitre and take thee much soap, thine iniquity is marked before the Most High; you cannot scrub your conscience clean, only Christ can.
precepts.point: Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God.” You can scrub the body with nitre and much soap and your iniquity is still marked before the Most High. You cannot scrub your conscience clean; only Christ can.

Water only washes the dirt off the skin. The evil in the mind is cleansed by Christ's baptism, the Holy Ghost the apostles laid hands on them to receive, which purifies your consciousness through his word.
